title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 54
paragraphs: They, then, were exhorting Amompharetos, the only one of the Lacedaemonians and Tegeans left behind. Meanwhile the Athenians were keeping themselves quietly in the place where they had been posted, knowing the Spartan spirit — that they tend to say one thing and mean another. When the army began to move, the Athenians sent a horseman from their own number to see whether the Spartans were attempting to set out, or whether they really had no intention of retreating, and they told him to ask Pausanias what they ought to do.
